newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP says would sell Dai Hung stake.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP says would sell Dai Hung stake.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd said on Friday it would be interested in any reasonble offer for its stake in the Dai Hung oil project in Vietnam.

"I think we would take any reasonable offer for Dai Hung," BHP chief executive John Prescott told a briefing after the release of first quarter results. "If somebody put an offer on the table we would look seriously at it," he said.

The Dai Hung field is owned by a consortium comprising BHP with a 43.75-percent stake, Malaysia's national oil company Petronas with 20 percent, Vietnam's state-owned PetroVietnam with 15 percent and Total SA and Sumitomo Corp with 10.625 percent each.

Asked if Petronas had expressed interest in BHP's Dai Hung stake, Prescott said: "We have a good relationship with Petronas and I'm sure if they had something in mind, I'll be happy to talk to them." Petronas had said earlier it had no plans to buy BHP's stake. BHP fully wrote down its A$151 million Dai Hung investment in its 1995/96 accounts.
